title: Portfolio pages slow and failing
summary: Portfolio and positions pages became slow and error‑prone beginning ~14:41 UTC when the external quotes‑vendor latency rose sharply, causing market‑data‑service HTTPS calls (800 ms timeout) to time out and its circuit breaker to go half‑open. Downstream callers – portfolio‑service (gRPC 500 ms timeout) and orders‑service – received DEADLINE_EXCEEDED errors, which manifested as >2 s p99 latency, 5xx errors, and order rejections. The portfolio‑service v5.4.0 deploy occurred at 14:48 UTC, after the degradation had already started, and was ruled out as the primary cause. Confidence in the vendor‑latency hypothesis (HYP‑1) is moderate (≈0.62). The exact reason for the vendor slowdown (throttling, internal outage, network path) remains unknown.

hypothesis.mechanism: An increase in latency or throttling at the external quotes‑vendor caused market‑data‑service HTTPS calls (800 ms timeout) to time out. The service’s circuit breaker went half‑open, so downstream callers (portfolio‑service via gRPC 500 ms timeout and orders‑service) received DEADLINE_EXCEEDED errors. This cascaded into elevated portfolio‑service latency and 5xx errors, and order rejections at orders‑service.
predictions: Minute‑resolution market‑data‑service latency_p99_ms and error_rate will show a rise beginning ~14:40 UTC.
Quotes‑vendor side metrics (if available) would show increased latency or throttling at the same time.

objections.detail: Portfolio‑service v5.4.0 deployed at 14:48 UTC, after latency/error spikes began at 14:41‑14:45 UTC (OBS‑24).

hypothesis.mechanism: A transient network or routing issue between market‑data‑service and the quotes‑vendor increased round‑trip latency beyond the 800 ms timeout, causing the same cascade of DEADLINE_EXCEEDED errors to portfolio‑service and orders‑service.
predictions: Network‑level metrics (e.g., packet loss, RTT) between market‑data‑service and quotes‑vendor would show a spike at ~14:40 UTC.
Restarting market‑data‑service instances would not resolve the issue until the network path recovers.
Portfolio‑service internal latency breakdown would show the gRPC client latency dominating the >2 s p99.

objections.detail: HYP‑1 (quotes‑vendor latency/throttling) explains all observed symptoms with direct log and metric evidence; a generic network failure has not been ruled out but lacks supporting data.

hypothesis.mechanism: A sudden burst of requests (perhaps from portfolio‑service) exhausted market‑data‑service thread‑pool or connection‑pool, causing its outbound HTTPS calls to quotes‑vendor to timeout and the circuit breaker to half‑open.

actions.description: Increase the market‑data‑service → quotes‑vendor timeout and/or add a short‑circuit fallback (e.g., cached quote) to prevent cascading DEADLINE_EXCEEDED errors.
actions.rationale: Current 800 ms timeout is too tight for observed vendor latency spikes; a higher timeout or cached fallback buys time for upstream services.

actions.description: Raise portfolio‑service gRPC timeout to market‑data‑service (currently 500 ms) and implement retry/back‑off with circuit‑breaker awareness.
actions.rationale: Portfolio‑service is the first downstream consumer; a modest timeout increase reduces 5xx errors while the vendor issue is resolved.

actions.description: Add explicit resilience patterns (timeout, retry, bulkhead, fallback) for the market‑data‑service → quotes‑vendor call and expose per‑dependency latency metrics.
actions.rationale: Hard‑coded 800 ms timeout and lack of observability made the cascade invisible until it impacted customers.
